title: Pine Labs Helpdesk — BIN Series API Contract
version: Bin Series priority task — bulk upload + stats + resolve-batch + search/filter + dynamic/custom columns + export + version history + API naming/route rename

authentication.currentStatus: Authentication boundary implemented; production identity-provider validation remains pending Pine Labs SSO/OIDC configuration. Every request is currently rejected with 401 AUTH_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED regardless of the token supplied, until a real provider is wired up.
authentication.actorHandling: There is no client-suppliable actor/user field anywhere in these APIs. The acting user for audit logging and updatedBy is always derived server-side from the authenticated caller.

errorFormat.description: Every error response (any non-2xx) uses this envelope.

commonErrorCodes.meaning: Real identity provider not yet configured (current state for every token).
Request shape/format failed schema validation (bad field type, pattern, required field missing/blank).
No BIN record exists for the given id / (binIin, merchantPrefix) pair.
A BIN record already exists with this exact (binIin, merchantPrefix).
merchantId was supplied but does not reference an existing merchant.
On update: instanceName was explicitly sent as null, or the update would leave the record without one.

A customFields key on create/update, or a columnId on PATCH /custom-columns/{columnId}/rename, does not reference an existing custom column. (422 on create/update since it's a request-body validation problem; 404 on PATCH /custom-columns/{columnId}/rename since the id is a path parameter identifying a specific resource.)
POST /custom-columns/create or PATCH /custom-columns/{columnId}/rename would result in a custom column name that already exists (case-insensitive).

notes.bulkUploadPerRowOutcomes: POST /bulk-upload never fails the whole batch for one bad row — see that endpoint's own errorResponses/notes for its per-row failedRows/skippedRows model instead of request-level error codes.
notes.apiNamingTask: Every Bin Series route path was renamed once (API Naming task) so its purpose reads directly from the URL — see each endpoint's own `renamedFrom` field for its prior path. This was a pure URL rename: no request/response schema, business logic, database behavior, or authentication changed. `/export` and `/bulk-upload` were kept as-is (already self-explanatory).

BinRecordResponse.description: Returned by list, lookup, create, and update.

merchantId.note: Soft link to the merchants table (SOP/classification domain). Not a business-name field.

instanceName.note: Null for legacy records created before this field existed (all 611 originally seeded records).

customFields.note: ALWAYS present, ALWAYS an object (never null) — default {}. Keyed by each custom column's immutable `key` (see CustomColumnResponse), never by its display `name`. Every currently-registered custom column that has never been given a value for this row is still present here as an empty string, since POST /bin-series/custom-columns/create backfills every existing row at creation time.

updatedBy.note: Name of the user who last created/updated this record via the write APIs. Null if never touched by them (e.g. seeded data).

merchantId.rule: if supplied, must reference an existing merchant

instanceName.rule: must not be missing, null, empty, or whitespace-only; trimmed server-side

customFields.rule: every key MUST reference an existing custom column's `key` (422 BIN_CUSTOM_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND otherwise); omit entirely for a row with no custom values yet

UpdateBinRecordRequest.description: Partial update — every field optional. Omitting a field leaves it unchanged.

merchantId.rule: if present, must reference an existing merchant

instanceName.rule: omit = leave unchanged; explicit null is REJECTED (422 BIN_INSTANCE_NAME_REQUIRED); empty/whitespace REJECTED (422 VALIDATION_ERROR); if this update changes ANY field and the record has no instanceName yet, one must be supplied in this same request

customFields.rule: MERGES into the existing customFields — only the keys you include change, every other existing key is left untouched. Every key MUST reference an existing custom column's `key` (422 BIN_CUSTOM_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND otherwise). An empty string is a valid value (a deliberate 'cleared' state) — there is no way to remove a key entirely, matching the frontend's own EditableCell, which never sends anything but a trimmed string.

BulkUploadRequest.description: Backs the frontend's BinTable "Import Data" upload flow (UploadSheetModal.jsx) — mode maps to that modal's two tabs. JSON body, not multipart: the frontend already parses CSV/XLSX into row objects client-side (utils/csv.js) before any call to this endpoint would happen.

instanceName.rule: must not be missing, null, empty, or whitespace-only
instanceName.note: Applied to every row created in addNew mode. In updateExisting mode, only backfilled onto matched rows that don't already have an instanceName — never overwrites an existing value. NOT collected by the current UploadSheetModal.jsx — see openQuestionsForProduct.

BulkUploadRow.description: All fields optional at the schema level — which ones are actually required depends on `mode` and the matching strategy (validated per-row in the service, not rejected at the request level).

issuer.note: addNew: required, non-blank. updateExisting: used as the fallback match key when binIin/merchantPrefix are absent (only if it resolves to exactly one existing record); if present and non-blank it also overwrites the target's issuer once matched.

cardProgramGroupName.note: addNew: required, non-blank. updateExisting: blank/omitted = leave unchanged.

binIin.note: addNew: required, exactly 6 digits. updateExisting: PRIMARY match key (with merchantPrefix) when both are present — never itself updated.

merchantPrefix.note: addNew: required, exactly 3 digits. updateExisting: other half of the PRIMARY match key — never itself updated.

merchantId.note: If present, must reference an existing merchant.

BulkUploadRowNote.description: One entry in failedRows or skippedRows.

rowIndex.note: 0-indexed position in the submitted rows array.

BinSeriesStatsResponse.description: Backs the frontend's StatCards on the BIN Series page (src/components/dashboard/StatCards.jsx) — today computed client-side from the full local mock array.

totalRecords.note: COUNT(*) over the whole bin_records table — not paginated/filtered.

ResolveBatchRequest.description: Backs BulkLookupModal.jsx (opened from both BinResolver.jsx and BinTable.jsx).

cards.note: Raw card number strings in any format — non-digit characters (spaces, hyphens, etc.) are stripped before matching. Empty/blank/too-short strings are valid entries — they simply resolve to matched:false, never rejected individually.

ResolveBatchResultItem.description: One entry per input card, same order, duplicates preserved — never dropped, never merged.

input.note: The raw, TRIMMED original input string, verbatim — never reformatted. (The frontend's own local resolve() reformats successfully-parsed cards as "{bin} {prefix}"; this API deliberately returns the literal input instead, for an unambiguous contract — the frontend can still reformat it for display however it likes.)

binIin.note: The 6-digit BIN extracted from input, if at least 6 digits were present — set regardless of match outcome.

merchantPrefix.note: The 3-digit prefix extracted from input, ONLY if a full 3 digits were present — set regardless of match outcome. A partial (1-2 digit) prefix is never echoed back as if complete.

CustomColumnResponse.description: Returned by GET /bin-series/custom-columns, POST .../custom-columns/create, and PATCH .../custom-columns/{id}/rename. Backs BinTable.jsx's column registry (AddColumnModal.jsx / EditableHeader.jsx).

key.note: IMMUTABLE — set once at creation to the column's initial (trimmed, whitespace-collapsed) name, never changes again even if the column is renamed. This is the key every bin_records.customFields entry for this column is stored under.

name.note: The current display label — the only thing PATCH /custom-columns/{columnId}/rename changes. Unique (case-insensitive) across all custom columns, same as `key` at creation time.

displayOrder.note: Creation sequence (1, 2, 3, ...) — matches BinTable.jsx, which always appends a new column after every existing one. There is no reorder capability in the frontend, so this value never changes after creation.

updatedBy.note: Name of the user who created or most recently renamed this column.

name.rule: non-blank after trim/whitespace-collapse; must not already exist (case-insensitive)

defaultValue.note: If supplied, backfilled onto EVERY existing bin_records row as this column's initial value (in the same transaction as the column's creation). If omitted, every existing row gets an empty string for this column instead — matches AddColumnModal.jsx's 'applied to all N existing records at once' behavior exactly.

name.rule: non-blank after trim/whitespace-collapse; must not already exist on another column (case-insensitive)

HistoryActor.description: Deliberately just id + name (no email) — BinTable.jsx's Version History UI never displays an email anywhere, unlike the generic GET /api/v1/revisions' fuller user object.

BinSeriesHistoryEntry.description: One entry in GET /api/v1/bin-series/version-history. ALWAYS carries its full before/after snapshot when one exists — the frontend's click-to-preview (ChangePreviewModal.jsx) re-uses this SAME object, never a second request.

action.note: NOT the raw revisions.action_type (create/update/delete/upload only) — 'column' (a bin_custom_column create) and 'rename' (a bin_custom_column update) are derived from the (entityType, raw action_type) pair, matching the approved frontend's own 6-way local vocabulary exactly (VersionHistoryModal.jsx's actionMeta / ChangePreviewModal.jsx's typeMeta).

entityId.note: The affected BIN record's or custom column's id — a soft reference (not a FK), so it survives the entity's own deletion.

fieldsChanged.note: Present for update/rename/bulk-upload-update entries: { "<Field Label>": { "from": ..., "to": ... } }. Null for create/delete/column-create (nothing to diff).

before.note: Complete pre-change state, or null if none existed (create) or none was captured (a revision written before this task shipped — NEVER reconstructed from current DB state in that case). Shape matches BinRecordResponse (minus updatedBy/updatedAt) for bin_record entries, or CustomColumnResponse (minus updatedBy/updatedAt) for bin_custom_column entries.

after.note: Complete post-change state, or null if the entity no longer exists (delete) or wasn't captured. Same shape rules as `before`.

total.note: Total matching revisions (bin_record + bin_custom_column) regardless of `limit` — informational only, NOT a page count; there is no true pagination on this endpoint (see the endpoint's own notes).

endpoints.name: List BIN records
endpoints.description: Search & Filter task: the approved frontend (BinTable.jsx) has exactly ONE global search box — matching every field on a row, case-insensitive substring — and NO filter dropdowns or column-sort UI at all. This endpoint already covers that (and more, pre-existing from Part 7); the only gap found and fixed was `search` not covering `instanceName`, now added. `issuer`/`cardProgramGroupName` exact filters and `sortBy`/`sortOrder` have no current frontend trigger (no UI control sends them) — kept as-is from Part 7, neither removed nor further extended.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring (ILIKE '%term%') match, ORed across issuer, cardProgramGroupName, binIin, merchantPrefix, instanceName, and every customFields VALUE.
search.note: instanceName was added by the Search & Filter task; customFields VALUES (never keys/column names) were added by the Dynamic/Custom Columns task — matches the frontend's own per-row "search every field" behavior (Object.values(row), which iterates values only, never object keys). Deliberately does NOT search id/updatedAt (internal/audit fields, never meaningful search targets) or merchantId (frontend rows have no such field).

issuer.description: Exact, case-insensitive issuer filter. No current frontend UI triggers this (pre-existing from Part 7).

cardProgramGroupName.description: Exact, case-insensitive filter. No current frontend UI triggers this (pre-existing from Part 7).

sortBy.note: No current frontend UI triggers this — BinTable.jsx has no column-sort controls at all (pre-existing from Part 7).

endpoints.name: Export BIN records (CSV)
endpoints.description: Backs the frontend's Export button (BinTable.jsx's exportSheet() -> utils/csv.js). CONFIRMED BY INSPECTION: the approved Export button downloads `data` — the FULL local dataset — not the search-box-filtered `rows`, not the current page, and there is no row-selection UI at all (no checkboxes anywhere in BinTable.jsx). This endpoint therefore returns EVERY matching row in one response; there is deliberately no page/pageSize parameter. `search`/`issuer`/`cardProgramGroupName` are accepted for forward integration (identical semantics to, and reusing the same repository filter as, GET /api/v1/bin-series/list) even though today's approved frontend calls Export with none of them — calling this endpoint with no query parameters reproduces the button's current behavior exactly.

search.description: Identical semantics to GET /api/v1/bin-series/list's `search` (issuer, cardProgramGroupName, binIin, merchantPrefix, instanceName, and every customFields VALUE).

issuer.description: Exact, case-insensitive issuer filter — same as GET /api/v1/bin-series/list.

cardProgramGroupName.description: Exact, case-insensitive filter — same as GET /api/v1/bin-series/list.

successResponse.description: A raw CSV document, NOT a JSON envelope. Rows ordered by id ascending (a deterministic default — the frontend's own local array has no meaningful sort order of its own to replicate). Header row is always present, even when zero rows match.

columns.order: Issuer, Card Program Group Name, BIN / IIN Code, Merchant Prefix, <every custom column in display order, by its current NAME>, Updated By, Updated At
columns.note: Exactly BinTable.jsx's own `exportColumns` order — base fields (insertion order from the frontend's row shape), then any custom columns (addColumn() always inserts a new one before the trailing audit pair, never after), then Updated By / Updated At last. `merchantId` and `instanceName` are deliberately NOT included: the frontend's local mock row objects never had those fields, so they never appear in Object.keys(row) and never reach the real exported CSV either — see openQuestionsForProduct.

headerLabels.baseColumns: FIXED: Issuer, Card Program Group Name, BIN / IIN Code, Merchant Prefix, Updated By, Updated At — matches BinTable.jsx's baseColumnLabels exactly. NOT affected by a client's local base-column rename, since base-column renames are frontend-only and never persisted to the backend (confirmed by the Dynamic/Custom Columns task) — the server has no way to know about a rename it was never told about.
headerLabels.customColumns: Each custom column's CURRENT, PERSISTED `name` (from bin_custom_columns, same registry GET /bin-series/custom-columns, POST .../create, and PATCH .../rename use) — a custom-column rename IS a real backend write, so it's correctly reflected on the next export.

csvFormat.quoting: RFC4180-style: a value is wrapped in double quotes (with internal quotes doubled) only if it contains a comma, double quote, or newline — matches utils/csv.js's csvEscape exactly (Python's csv module default QUOTE_MINIMAL dialect).
csvFormat.emptyValues: Represented as an empty (unquoted) field — never omitted, never null, never a placeholder like 'N/A'.
csvFormat.encoding: UTF-8, no byte-order-mark (the frontend's Blob doesn't add one either).

endpoints.audit: None — read-only, same as GET /api/v1/bin-series/list and GET /lookup. Export was already a pure client-side download with no backend involvement; nothing about adding a server-side endpoint for the same read makes it an auditable write.

endpoints.name: Bin Series Version History
endpoints.description: Backs BinTable.jsx's 'Version History' button (VersionHistoryModal.jsx / ChangePreviewModal.jsx). GLOBAL to the whole Bin Series table, NOT scoped to one record — confirmed by inspection there is no per-row history trigger anywhere in the approved frontend (RowActionsMenu.jsx has no history action at all), just one table-wide button. DISTINCT from the existing generic GET /api/v1/revisions (which covers ALL entity types with no before/after snapshots): this endpoint is scoped to exactly bin_record + bin_custom_column revisions and returns full before/after state for each. Both read the SAME underlying `revisions` table — this is not a second audit system, only a second, richer read of it. There is deliberately NO separate detail/'by id' endpoint: confirmed by inspection that clicking a history entry (ChangePreviewModal.jsx) reads the SAME entry object already in the list, never a second request — so every entry here already carries everything a detail view would need.

limit.description: Max entries to return, newest first. Default 5 matches the frontend's own VersionHistoryModal, which always slices `entries.slice(0, 5)` out of its local changeLog — there is no 'load more' UI, so this is a plain LIMIT, not page/pageSize pagination.

items.changeDescription: Issuer changed from Aurora Retail to Aurora Retail Ltd

notes: A revision created BEFORE this task shipped has no before/after snapshot in its stored metadata — its entry's `before`/`after` are simply null, NEVER reconstructed from current bin_records/bin_custom_columns state. Its `fieldsChanged`/`changeDescription`/`actor`/`occurredAt` are still fully populated (those existed already).

A deleted BIN record's history remains fully available: the entry's `before` snapshot was captured and persisted at delete time, and this endpoint only ever reads `revisions` — it never queries bin_records to reconstruct anything, so a since-deleted row's history is exactly as complete as any other entry's.

Bulk upload rows create action='upload' entries (never 'create'/'update') — same convention as the existing bulk-upload audit trail; each row's own before/after snapshot is included exactly like a single-row create/update would have.
endpoints.audit: None — read-only. This endpoint only reads existing revisions, it never writes one.

endpoints.name: Resolve one BIN record
endpoints.description: Exact (binIin, merchantPrefix) lookup only. Never returns a partial match.

errorResponses.when: no record matches the exact pair

endpoints.name: BIN Series stats
endpoints.description: Backs the frontend's StatCards on the BIN Series page (Total Records / Issuers / Card Programs), today computed client-side from the full local mock array. Always a whole-table aggregate — no pagination, no filters.

endpoints.name: Bulk/multi-card resolve
endpoints.description: Backs BulkLookupModal.jsx (opened from both BinResolver.jsx and BinTable.jsx) — resolve many card numbers in one request. MATCHING RULE is a documented SUPERSET of GET /lookup's rule, not a second inconsistent algorithm: exact (binIin, merchantPrefix) match when a full 3 prefix digits are present; otherwise, if the BIN uniquely identifies exactly one existing record, resolves to it anyway (never guesses among 2+ candidates) — exactly matching BulkLookupModal.jsx's own local resolve() function. Read-only: no actor, no audit revision, same as GET /lookup.

errorResponses.when: cards missing/absent, empty array, or over 1000 entries — rejects the WHOLE request

notes: Every input card gets exactly one result, in input order — duplicates and unmatched/malformed cards are never dropped, merged, or treated as errors.
A card with fewer than 6 usable digits (including a blank string) resolves to matched:false with binIin/merchantPrefix both null — never a 422.
`input` is always the raw trimmed original string, never reformatted — a deliberate difference from the frontend's own current local resolve() function (see ResolveBatchResultItem's note).
Max 1000 cards per request — no limit exists in the current frontend; this reuses the same cap already established for POST /bulk-upload rather than inventing a new number.

endpoints.name: Create BIN record

errorResponses.when: missing/blank issuer, cardProgramGroupName, or instanceName; malformed binIin/merchantPrefix
merchantId supplied but does not exist
a customFields key does not reference an existing custom column

endpoints.audit: Creates a revision: action=create, entityType=bin_record. Actor is always the authenticated caller, never client-supplied.

endpoints.name: Bulk upload BIN records
endpoints.description: Backs the frontend's BIN table "Import Data" button (UploadSheetModal.jsx). MATCHING KEY IS HYBRID: (binIin, merchantPrefix) is used when a row supplies both (the real, DB-unique key); otherwise the row falls back to an issuer-name match, but ONLY if that issuer matches exactly one existing record — an issuer matching 2+ records fails that row as ambiguous rather than guessing. This exists because the frontend's current client-side updateExisting() matches by issuer alone, and issuer is not globally unique (the frontend's own seed data has 'Aurora Retail' twice, at two different binIin/merchantPrefix pairs).

updateExistingByIssuerFallbackExample.note: Only matches if 'Aurora Retail' is unique in the database — it is NOT in the real seed data (two rows share that issuer), so this exact example would fail as ambiguous against real data.

errorResponses.when: instanceName missing/blank, mode invalid/missing, or rows array empty/absent/over 1000 entries — these reject the WHOLE request (request-shape problems, not per-row)

notes: Per-row outcomes never reject the whole request — see failedRows (validation problem, ambiguous match, or write conflict) and skippedRows (updateExisting only: no matching row found, or nothing actually changed) in the response instead.

addNew: duplicate (binIin, merchantPrefix) — whether against an existing DB row or another row earlier in the same batch — fails that row only, with reason 'A BIN record already exists...'. Issuer duplication is NOT an error for addNew.
updateExisting: a row with no matching (binIin, merchantPrefix) or issuer is reported in skippedRows and is NEVER created — use mode=addNew for that.
updateExisting: only non-blank fields in a row are applied; binIin/merchantPrefix in a row are used ONLY to find the record when both are present, never to change it.
updateExisting: if two rows in the same batch resolve to the same existing record, they are applied in order — the later row's values win.
updateExisting: the batch-level instanceName only fills in a matched row that has none yet — it never overwrites a row's existing instanceName.
endpoints.audit: One revision PER successfully written row (not one for the whole batch): action=upload, entityType=bin_record — deliberately 'upload', not 'create'/'update', so bulk-import events stay distinguishable from manual single-row edits in revision history. Actor is always the authenticated caller. Each row's write + its revision are atomic with each other (one savepoint per row) — a mid-batch failure only rolls back that one row, never the rows before or after it.

endpoints.name: Update BIN record

requestBody.description: Partial update — send only the fields you want to change.

errorResponses.when: malformed binIin/merchantPrefix, or instanceName sent as empty/whitespace
merchantId supplied but does not exist
a customFields key does not reference an existing custom column
instanceName sent as explicit null, OR this update changes something while the record still has no instanceName
changing binIin/merchantPrefix would collide with another record

notes: A request that changes nothing (resends identical values) is a no-op: 200 OK, no audit revision created, updatedBy/updatedAt untouched.
instanceName can be omitted if the record already has one and you're only changing other fields.
instanceName cannot be omitted if the record currently has none AND you are changing any other field in this same request — must be supplied together.
endpoints.audit: Creates a revision only if something actually changed: action=update, entityType=bin_record, change description lists every changed field (e.g. 'Issuer changed from X to Y; instance name changed from A to B'). Actor is always the authenticated caller.

endpoints.name: Delete BIN record
endpoints.audit: Creates a revision: action=delete, entityType=bin_record, entityId=the deleted record's former id (soft reference, not a FK — survives the record's deletion). Actor is always the authenticated caller.

endpoints.name: List custom columns
endpoints.description: Backs BinTable.jsx's column registry. Returns every custom column in display order (creation sequence — the frontend always appends new columns after existing ones; there is no reorder capability, so this order never changes after creation).

endpoints.name: Create custom column
endpoints.description: Backs AddColumnModal.jsx. Creates a new custom column and, if defaultValue is supplied, backfills it onto EVERY existing bin_records row in the same transaction (else every existing row gets an empty string for this column) — matches AddColumnModal.jsx's 'applied to all N existing records at once' behavior exactly. The new column's `key` is set once, permanently, to the initial (trimmed/whitespace-collapsed) `name` — renaming later never changes it.

errorResponses.when: a custom column with this name (case-insensitive) already exists

endpoints.audit: Creates a revision: action=create, entityType=bin_custom_column. Actor is always the authenticated caller. The column-metadata insert and the existing-row backfill are one atomic transaction — never a partially-applied column.

endpoints.name: Rename custom column
endpoints.description: Backs EditableHeader.jsx's column rename. Changes ONLY the column's display `name` — its `key` (and therefore every bin_records.customFields value already stored under it) is completely untouched, exactly matching BinTable.jsx's renameColumn(). Resending the current name is a no-op: 200 OK, no audit revision.

errorResponses.when: another custom column already has this name (case-insensitive)

endpoints.audit: Creates a revision only if the name actually changed: action=update, entityType=bin_custom_column. Actor is always the authenticated caller.

notImplemented.description: Explicitly out of scope so far — do not assume these exist.
items: Bulk single-column update (no endpoint) — e.g. ColumnUploadModal.jsx's per-column bulk value upload
Delete a custom column — the frontend has no delete-column capability at all, so no DELETE /bin-series/custom-columns/{columnId} endpoint exists
Reorder custom columns — the frontend has no reorder UI, so displayOrder is pure creation sequence and there is no endpoint to change it

Rename a BASE column (issuer, cardProgramGroupName, binIin, merchantPrefix, merchantId, instanceName) — confirmed frontend-only/never persisted for base columns either, so no backend change was made for this

A separate Version History 'detail' / 'get one revision' endpoint (e.g. GET /bin-series/version-history/{revisionId}) — confirmed by inspection that ChangePreviewModal.jsx re-uses the SAME entry object already returned by the list, never a second request, so GET /bin-series/version-history's own entries already carry everything a detail view would need
Per-record Version History (e.g. GET /bin-series/{binRecordId}/version-history) — confirmed the approved frontend's Version History panel is GLOBAL to the whole table, not scoped to one row
SOP write APIs of any kind (SOP is currently read-only: GET sheet detail, GET sheet rows, GET common escalation)

openQuestionsForProduct: Should 'issuer' be renamed to 'issuerName'? No field called 'merchantName' was found in the BIN domain to rename — 'issuer' already serves that role and matches the frontend's own field name.
Confirm the instanceName-mandatory-on-update interpretation: a real write must leave the record with a non-blank instanceName, but omitting it is fine if the record already has one.
What should instanceName actually reference long-term (currently a free-text string, no backend 'instances' table exists)?

BLOCKER for real frontend integration: UploadSheetModal.jsx collects no instanceName at all today (batch-level or per-row) — the bulk-upload endpoint requires one. Frontend work is needed to add this before the Import Data flow can actually call this endpoint.

The current updateExisting() in BinTable.jsx matches by issuer only; the backend now supports (binIin, merchantPrefix) as the primary key with issuer as a safe fallback — frontend would need to start sending binIin/merchantPrefix per row (it already has this data available from formColumns) to use the safer path.

GET /bin-series/export deliberately omits merchantId and instanceName from the CSV, matching the approved frontend's local mock row shape exactly (data/binSeries.js has neither field) — same underlying mismatch already flagged above for instanceName/merchantId generally. If product wants these two fields in the exported CSV, the frontend's own row shape (and therefore its Export button) would need to grow them first — this endpoint was built to replicate today's approved Export behavior, not to unilaterally add columns the UI has never shown.
